newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus says Cathay problems engine only.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says Cathay problems engine only.

text.p: Technical problems which have grounded a fleet of Airbus A330 planes at Asian airline Cathay Pacific are engine-related and do not affect the airframe, European consortium Airbus Industrie said on Monday.

Hong Kong flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) grounded on Saturday their fleet of 15 Airbus A330-300 wide-body planes, after a Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engine failed on a Dragonair A330.

"This is a direct engine-related problem, exclusively a Rolls problem," an Airbus spokeswoman said. "It is not related to the airframe and does not affect other A330s in service or any other Airbus type."
"We are of course assisting as much as we can," she added. "We are confident it will be sorted out quickly."
Rolls Royce said on Friday it had identified the problem, which was related to the gearbox bearings, and is replacing the components.
French equipment supplier Hispano Suiza declined to comment on a newspaper report its bearings supplied to Rolls were involved.
Garuda Indonesia Airways also flies the A330 but has different Rolls engines from those fitted on Cathay Pacific and Dragonair's fleet, she said.
Garuda has not suspended its A330s, although Hong Kong's civil aviation authority urged on Monday the Indonesian company to ground its planes on engine worries.

The groundings on Saturday followed an emergency landing by a Dragonair A330-300 at Subic Bay in the Philippines on Friday after the plane developed trouble in one of its two Rolls-Royce Trent engines.

Cathay Pacific was the launch customer for the Rolls-powered A330, which was delivered with great ceremony and featured the airline's livery redesign. The Rolls-equipped A330 was hailed as boosting the plane's European content.
A Cathay spokesman said the company expected to cancel 18 flights on Monday, the same number as Sunday and Saturday. The airline expects flights to resume in three weeks.
Dragonair is 25.5 percent owned by Cathay and flies four A330-300s.
It was the fifth time since November that a Cathay Pacific or Dragonair A330-300 had made a single-engine landing.
Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
